prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Do you have a fresh white wine from a small maker that isn't too heavy and tastes like honey and butter?"

List A:
Wine 1: Riesling, US, $18. Tasting note: "This has aromas of yellow peach and butter. Straightforward flavors faintly resemble peach, with more of the buttery richness that seems unusual for this variety. It's a good, basic, full-bodied white wine."
Wine 2: Chardonnay, US, $42. Tasting note: "Made in small amounts, this floral, tangy and richly textured white wine offers a depth of honey and caramel that overpowers the prettier, more mineral-driven aspects lurking in the underbelly of body. Youthful, it should come around."
Wine 3: Sparkling Blend, Spain, $15. Tasting note: "White-fruit aromas are without frills. Like the nose, this wine feels fresh and clean. Flavors of white peach and slightly underripe honeydew are mild and don't force anything on a pleasant finish."
Wine 4: Gros and Petit Manseng, France, $22. Tasting note: "This honeyed white wine made from late-harvest grapes is both intensely rich and so fresh and crisp. Its acidity cuts through the ripe apricot and candied orange flavors, creating a balance that will allow it to age. Drink from 2019."
Wine 5: Chardonnay, US, $13. Tasting note: "One of the more reliable, big-production brands in the market right now, this wine shows fresh white flowers, with just a dollop of vanilla butter and a touch of wet stone on the nose. There is decent verve to the evenly presented and light palate, with flavors of cooked apples and sea salt."

List B:
Wine 1: Verdelho, US, $15. Tasting note: "With mouthwatering crispness and a pleasantly bitter, minerally tone, this fine, dry white wine is versatile at the table. It has savory flavors of citrus fruits, honeysuckle flowers and white pepper."
Wine 2: Pinot Grigio, US, $10. Tasting note: "Drink this dryish wine with almost anything that calls for a light-bodied, crisp white, and don't worry about it. It has savory citrus flavors, with a pleasant hint of vanilla honey."
Wine 3: Chardonnay, US, $10. Tasting note: "This is a basic white wine with a few quirks. It smells floral and appley, and tastes quite dry and a bit sharp while carrying a candylike marshmallow note."
Wine 4: Riesling, US, $9. Tasting note: "If you like your white wines fruity and sweet, this one's for you. It has pretty flavors of peaches, honey and spices."
Wine 5: White Blend, US, $21. Tasting note: "this full-bodied white wine stresses complexity, weight and viscosity. It smells like blanched almonds and candle wax, and tastes rich, almost heavy."
